b: Earlier this year, I switched jobs. I had a few weeks of unused vacation at my former role, so I "vacationed out" for 4 weeks, which should have ended 6 weeks ago. When I started my new role, I figured out how much I would have contributed to 401k, HSA, and dependent FSA based on my correct end date, and put in what would be needed to max them out at my new job.

Since then, the previous employer has kept paying me as if I worked there - depositing money in my account every 2 weeks including withholding for, and contributing to, my 401k, HSA, and dependent care FSA.

I've contacted them several times to let them know, but other an them acknowledging they received my emails they don't seem to be doing anything, and I just got notice from my bank another check is being deposited tomorrow.

I've kept the money deposited in my bank account to give it back, but since they are taking money out to add to my 401k, HSA, and dependent care FSA, adding in my contributions from the current employer means each of these is now over the limit for 2026 - and that's not counting future contributions I don't have time to stop since my current role takes two months to update contribution amounts.

I'm sure the old company will eventually unwind everything, but considering that 6 weeks after first notifying them I'm getting paychecks and the HR team takes off 3 of the remaining 7 weeks in 2026, I'm beginning to get worried it might not be fixed this calendar year, and I'll be over the limits for 2026 on Jan 1, 2027.

Is there anything I can do to protect myself from paying tax on excess contributions, only to then have those contributions taken back, if the old company has not fully unwound everything prior to Jan 1?
